checkpoints.question: What is gimbal lock?
checkpoints.model_answer: At pitch plus or minus 90 degrees, the ZYX Euler-angle representation is singular: roll and yaw no longer describe independent infinitesimal rotations. The Duckiedrone can still rotate about all three physical axes.

checkpoints.question: Which axes do roll, pitch, and yaw describe in this notebook?
checkpoints.model_answer: Read about the fixed world axes, the ZYX product applies roll about world x first, then pitch about world y, then yaw about world z. Read about the Duckiedrone's own axes, the same product applies yaw first, then pitch about the turned y axis, then roll about the turned x axis. Both readings give the same rotation matrix, so stating the axes and their order makes the convention unambiguous.

evidence.label: Euler angles and the rotation matrix

checkpoints.question: Why does the order of roll, pitch, and yaw rotations matter?
checkpoints.model_answer: Three-dimensional rotations generally do not commute, so changing their order changes the resulting orientation. This notebook uses the ZYX convention.

evidence.label: Euler angles and the rotation matrix

checkpoints.question: An IMU vector is already expressed in body-frame components. Which rotation maps it into world-frame components?
checkpoints.model_answer: R_WB maps the body-frame components into world-frame components. Gravity correction is a separate step when recovering linear acceleration.

evidence.label: The rotation matrix is a representation too
